label: absolute position t>=6 up to and including the <DEL> step (late input-phase position counter)
explanation: Fires on every input-phase step at absolute position t >= 6 (original tokens 7-9) and on the <DEL> step when it falls at t >= 6 (L >= 6), regardless of token identity. Silent at t <= 5 (so never for L <= 5, apart from rare weak t=5 hits) and essentially silent throughout the copy phase. Magnitude rises roughly linearly with absolute t (~0.2 of max at t=6, ~0.5 at t=7, ~0.75 at t=8, ~1.0 at t=9), so the <DEL> step is the peak only because it is the latest step; an L=6 <DEL> at t=6 is weak (~0.2). Token identity, previous tokens and digit content have no meaningful effect.

issues: No systematic problems. On the test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.999, F1 0.9995, mass recall 0.99986, and there are 0 false positives.

The 854 missed steps hold about 0.0% of activation mass. They are almost all weak <DEL> steps at t=5 (L=5, about 0.05-0.07 of max), which the explanation already admits as 'rare weak t=5 hits'. The one exception is a single 0.32 hit on the first copy step. There are also about 105 tiny copy-phase hits at t=10 (recall_idx 1, about 0.06 of max).

The magnitude claims check out against the profile examples. Activation is about 0.2 of max at t=6, 0.5 at t=7, 0.75 at t=8 and up to 1.0 at the t=9 <DEL>. The L=6 <DEL> at t=6 is about 0.2. The <DEL> step reads slightly higher than an original token at the same t (for example 0.78-0.80 at t=8), but the difference is small.
Token identity has no effect: in_tok rates are flat at 0.084-0.085 across letters, and orig_idx 6-8 fires at a rate of 1.000.
